brief.angle: Streaming a static phone screen for one hour sends 216,000 full frames, but filtering unchanged pixels reduces the payload by 99 percent.
brief.measure: Comparing uncompressed 60 FPS video frame transmission against delta-only frame updates over a 60-minute screen session.
brief.calc: 60 frames/sec * 3600 sec = 216,000 frames vs 1 keyframe + 215,999 delta frames (~1% relative byte size).
sources: Repository documentation for dsh-see-now frame filtering logic

spec.title: Static screen waste
spec.summary: Streaming a static phone screen for one hour sends two hundred sixteen thousand frames, but delta filtering reduces the payload by ninety nine percent.
sources: Repository documentation for dsh-see-now frame filtering logic

beats.say: A static phone screen sends two hundred sixteen thousand frames per hour.
Sixty frames multiply by thirty six hundred seconds.
Every single identical pixel travels across the network repeatedly.
One initial keyframe starts the stream.
The remaining two hundred fifteen thousand nine hundred ninety nine frames are deltas.
Unchanged pixels bypass the network entirely.
Filtering drops the payload size to one percent.
